item.title: Artemis II crew begins historic lunar flyby Monday
item.description: Four astronauts aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft are poised to sweep around the Moon on Monday, capping a five-day outbound journey and marking the first time humans have traveled to the lunar neighborhood since Apollo 17 in 1972. The Artemis II crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, and Mission Specialists Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen of the Canadian Space Agency — launched from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B on April 1 at 6:35 p.m. EDT aboard the Space Launch System rocket.

item.title: Trump's deadline for Iran to reopen Strait of Hormuz arrives Monday
item.description:
Global oil prices climbed again over the weekend, with U.S. crude rising above $114 per barrel and Brent crude topping $110, after President Donald Trump issued an expletive-laden ultimatum demanding Iran reopen the Strait of Hormuz by the end of Monday or face strikes on its civilian infrastructure.

The latest price spike comes as the U.S.-Iran conflict enters its sixth week with no resolution in sight, and as Trump's self-imposed April 6 deadline for Iran to restore access to the critical waterway arrives.

item.title: Study: 84% of fire-vulnerable species face rising wildfire risk by 2100
item.description: Climate-driven wildfires will place nearly 84 percent of fire-vulnerable species at heightened risk by 2100, according to a study published in Nature Climate Change on April 5. The research, led by Xiaoye Yang of the University of Gothenburg, offers one of the most comprehensive assessments to date of how shifting wildfire regimes could reshape threats to global biodiversity.

item.title: Physicists cool nanorotor to quantum ground state in two dimensions
item.description: A team of European physicists has cooled the rotational motion of a levitated silica nanorotor to its quantum ground state in two dimensions for the first time, a result that opens new paths for quantum sensing and tests of fundamental physics. The work, published in Nature Physics on April 6, represents a leap beyond previous experiments that managed the feat in only one rotational axis.

item.title: Pakistan brokers ceasefire plan as Trump's Iran deadline nears Tuesday
item.description: The United States, Iran, and a group of regional mediators are racing to finalize terms for a potential 45-day ceasefire aimed at preventing a dramatic escalation of the war, as President Donald Trump's latest ultimatum for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approaches Tuesday evening.

item.title: IRGC intelligence chief killed in US-Israeli strikes that left at least 34 dead
item.description: Coordinated airstrikes by the United States and Israel killed at least 34 people across Iran on Monday, the 38th day of the war, in attacks that struck Tehran, Qom, and the southern port city of Bandar-e Lengeh. Among the dead was Major General Seyed Majid Khademi, the head of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' intelligence organization, according to an official IRGC statement carried by Iran's Fars news agency.

item.title: Artemis II crew flies past the moon in historic flyby
item.description: As four astronauts sweep around the far side of the Moon on Monday, the historic Artemis II mission reaches its climax under the watch of two key figures on the ground: chief flight director Emily Nelson and mission manager Matthew Ramsey. The mission, which launched on April 1 from Kennedy Space Center, marks the first time humans have traveled to the Moon since Apollo 17 in 1972.

item.title: Iran accuses IAEA of inaction over Bushehr strikes
item.description:
A projectile strike hit near Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant on Saturday, killing a security guard and damaging an auxiliary building in what marked the fourth attack on the facility since the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran began on February 28, the International Atomic Energy Agency confirmed.

IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi expressed "deep concern" over the incident, stressing that "nuclear power plant sites or nearby areas must never be attacked" and warning that auxiliary buildings "may contain vital safety equipment". The agency reported no increase in radiation levels at the site.

item.title: Artemis II crew set to fly around the Moon on Monday
item.description:
Saudi Arabia has become the first Arab nation to participate in NASA's Artemis program after its domestically built Shams satellite was successfully deployed aboard the Space Launch System rocket as part of the Artemis II mission, the Saudi Space Agency confirmed over the weekend.

The satellite, formally designated Space Weather CubeSat-1 in NASA documentation, is a 12U CubeSat that hitched a ride as a secondary payload when Artemis II lifted off from Kennedy Space Center on April 1. The Saudi Space Agency announced initial contact with the satellite on April 3, revealing its Arabic name — Shams, meaning "sun" — and outlining its scientific objectives.

item.title: Study of 1,700 languages finds shared grammar rules
item.description: Despite the staggering diversity of the world's languages, many follow the same grammatical playbook. A large-scale study analyzing more than 1,700 languages has found that roughly one-third of long-proposed "linguistic universals" hold up under rigorous statistical testing, pointing to deep cognitive and communicative forces that shape how humans build language.

item.title: Chinese scientist reveals military uses for space solar project
item.description: A senior Chinese scientist behind Beijing's ambitious space-based solar power program has published a paper outlining how the technology could be adapted for military operations, including surveillance, electronic warfare, and communications control, offering a rare public acknowledgment of the dual-use potential of one of China's most prominent energy megaprojects.

item.title: OpenAI CFO questions Altman's push for late 2026 IPO
item.description:
A rift has emerged at the top of OpenAI over the timing and affordability of what could become one of the largest public listings in technology history. Chief Financial Officer Sarah Friar has privately questioned CEO Sam Altman's push to take the company public as early as the fourth quarter of 2026, warning that OpenAI may not be organizationally prepared for such a move, according to a report by The Information published Saturday.

Friar has also raised concerns about Altman's commitment to spend $600 billion on computing infrastructure over the next five years, citing doubts about whether the company's revenue trajectory can support purchases of that magnitude. The tensions between the two most senior figures overseeing OpenAI's finances and strategy represent an unusual public signal of internal friction at the world's most valuable startup.

item.title: China builds largest South China Sea island as US forces shift to Iran
item.description: China is carrying out its most ambitious island-building campaign in the South China Sea since 2017, rapidly transforming a once-submerged coral reef into what could become its largest military outpost in the disputed waterway — a push that analysts say has been enabled by Washington's deepening entanglement in the war with Iran.

item.title: Iran rejects ceasefire as Trump's Tuesday deadline nears
item.description: Iran on Monday formally rejected the latest ceasefire proposal aimed at ending the war between Tehran and the United States and Israel, instead delivering a 10-point counter-response through Pakistan that demands a permanent end to hostilities. The rejection comes as President Donald Trump's deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approaches Tuesday evening, with the president threatening to destroy Iranian power plants and bridges if no deal is reached.

item.title: Artemis II crew set to break human spaceflight distance record during lunar flyby
item.description: Four astronauts aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft are conducting a historic flyby of the moon on Monday, swinging around the far side of the lunar surface on Flight Day 6 of their approximately 10-day mission. The crew entered the moon's sphere of influence early Monday morning and is set to break the record for the farthest humans have ever traveled from Earth, surpassing the mark set by Apollo 13 more than 55 years ago.

item.title: US-Israeli strikes destroy AI data center at Tehran university
item.description: US and Israeli warplanes struck the data center at Tehran's Sharif University of Technology early Monday, destroying infrastructure that supports Iran's artificial intelligence platform, according to Anadolu Agency and Iranian state media reports. The predawn attack reduced the university's information and communications technology building to rubble, also damaging laboratories, faculty buildings, and the campus mosque.

item.title: NY Fed: Supply chain stress hit three-year high in March
item.description:
Global supply chain pressures intensified in March, reaching their highest point in more than three years, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York reported Monday in its latest Global Supply Chain Pressure Index release.

The GSCPI rose to 0.68 in March, up from a revised 0.54 in February, according to the data published by the New York Fed. A reading of zero represents normal supply chain conditions, while positive values indicate above-average strain. The March figure marks the index's highest level since early 2023, when pandemic-era disruptions were still unwinding.

item.title: Artemis II breaks Apollo 13's distance record during lunar flyby
item.description:
Four astronauts aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft shattered a 56-year-old record on Monday afternoon, traveling farther from Earth than any humans in history. At 1:56 p.m. EDT on April 6, 2026, the Artemis II crew surpassed the 248,655-mile mark set by Apollo 13 in April 1970, ultimately reaching a maximum distance of approximately 252,757 miles from Earth — more than 4,100 miles beyond the previous record.

The crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen — became the first humans to visit the moon's vicinity since Apollo 17 in December 1972.

item.title: Cambridge solar reactor turns plastic waste into hydrogen
item.description: Researchers at the University of Cambridge have developed a solar-powered reactor that uses acid recovered from spent car batteries to break down hard-to-recycle plastics into clean hydrogen fuel and valuable industrial chemicals. The results, published in the journal Joule, describe a process the team calls "solar-powered acid photoreforming" that could offer a cheaper, more sustainable path for dealing with plastic waste.

item.title: UN condemns Trump threats to bomb Iran civilian infrastructure
item.description:
The United Nations on Monday warned the United States that any strikes on Iranian civilian infrastructure would constitute a clear violation of international law, responding to President Donald Trump's escalating threats to destroy Iran's power plants and bridges if Tehran does not reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

"We were alarmed by the rhetoric seen in that social media post that threatened American attacks on power plants, bridges, and other infrastructure should Iran not agree to a deal," Stephane Dujarric, chief spokesman for UN Secretary-General António Guterres, said at a daily briefing on Monday. "Any attack on civilian infrastructure is a violation of international law, and a very clear one."
